KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Musical Chairs — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches musical chairs — the furniture game where walking feet only, and the last chair is the championship.

What is this?

Musical chairs is a music game with chairs in a circle: walk while the music plays, sit when it stops — and one chair leaves the circle every round.

What does it mean?

The game is stopping-on-a-signal with a prize attached, and losing a chair kindly — then getting the DJ job — is the emotional lesson under the noise.

What does the child need to know?

You need one chair per player, minus one, and music. The living-room rule: walking feet only, never running, said out loud every round like a referee.

Why this matters

It is freeze dance with chairs — the same stop-on-the-signal skill, plus the wild joy of diving for a seat.

What it teaches

Walking control, listening for the stop, quick choosing, and the losing-then-helping loop.

Words to learn

chairscirclewalkmusicstopsitround

Say this to your child

“"Walk, walk, walk — walking feet! Here comes the music stopping... SIT! One chair goes away... walk again!"”

Step by step

  1. Put the chairs in a circle facing outward — one fewer chair than players.
  2. Say the rule: walking feet only. Say it again. Say it every round.
  3. Start the music — everyone walks around the outside of the chairs.
  4. Stop the music — everybody finds a chair and SITS.
  5. The player left standing becomes the DJ for the next round, and one chair leaves the circle. Last two players, last one chair — and a rematch for the crown.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, a ring of chairs sits empty with music notes circling above — the chairs wait for the walking players, and the notes say the music could stop at any moment.

Ask your child

"What kind of feet do we use?" (walking feet) "What happens when the music stops?" (find a chair and sit) "What is the DJ&rsquo;s job?" (stop the music — and start it again)

What your child can say or do

Your child might dive for chairs with full-commitment somersaults, lose round one with thundercloud eyebrows and win round five with a victory lap, or DJ with theatrical suspense.

Out in the real world

Every birthday party with more chairs than games ends up here — the child who knows the walking-feet rule and the DJ-job kindness is the one everyone wants back next time.

Try it together

Kind version for threes: two chairs for the final two players and a shared win, arms raised together. Strict version for fives: one chair, one champion, rematch on request.

Understanding check

Ask: "How many chairs are there?" (one fewer than players) "What do we do when the music stops?" (sit!) "What does the left-standing player get to be?" (the DJ)
